title: HAVE GOT y HAS GOT
subtitle: Have got and has got · tener

map.center: Usamos HAVE GOT para decir lo que tenemos: cosas, familia, mascotas y cómo somos.

nodes.title: Afirmativa
items: I have got a bike. (Tengo una bici.)
She has got a dog. (Ella tiene un perro.)

nodes.title: Negativa
items: I haven't got a cat. (No tengo gato.)
He hasn't got a cat. (Él no tiene gato.)
haven't = have not · hasn't = has not

nodes.title: Consejo rápido
items: La edad NO va con have: I am nine.
Have got = cosas que tienes, no acciones.

mini.es: Completa con have got o has got.
mini.en: Complete with have got or has got.

explain.es: Have got significa tener. Lo usamos para hablar de las cosas que tenemos (una bici, un lápiz), de la familia (un hermano), de las mascotas (un perro) y de cómo somos (ojos azules, pelo largo).
explain.en: Have got means to have. We use it for things we own, family, pets and what we look like.

explain.title: 1 · Afirmativa
explain.es: Con I, you, we, they usamos have got. Con he, she, it (una sola persona, animal o cosa) usamos has got. La palabra got se queda siempre igual.
explain.en: With I, you, we, they we use have got. With he, she, it we use has got. The word got never changes.
formula: I / you / we / they + *have got* + a bike
he / she / it + *has got* + a bike

examples.en: My brother has got a big dog.
examples.es: Mi hermano tiene un perro grande.

explain.title: Las contracciones
head: Forma larga · Long
Forma corta · Short
explain.note: Ojo: she's got = she has got. Pero she's nine = she is nine. El apóstrofo puede ser has o is: mira si después viene got.
explain.note_en: Careful: 's can mean has or is. If got comes next, it means has.

explain.title: 2 · Negativa
explain.es: Para decir que no tenemos algo, ponemos not después de have / has: haven't got y hasn't got. ¡No usamos don't ni doesn't con have got, y tampoco decimos no!
explain.en: To say we don't have something, put not after have / has: haven't got and hasn't got. Don't use don't or no.
formula: I / you / we / they + *haven't got* + a cat
he / she / it + *hasn't got* + a cat

explain.title: 3 · Preguntas
explain.es: Para preguntar, ponemos Have o Has delante del sujeto y got detrás. ¡Es como un salto: el verbo salta al principio! (Así se vence al Verbo Saltarín.)
explain.en: To ask a question, put Have or Has before the subject and got after it.
formula: *Have* + I / you / we / they + *got* + a pen?

explain.title: 4 · Respuestas cortas
head: Pregunta · Question
Sí · Yes
No
explain.note: En la respuesta corta nunca ponemos got: Yes, I have got. → Yes, I have.

explain.title: Todo junto
head: Sujeto · Subject
✅ Afirmativa
⛔ Negativa
❓ Pregunta
💬 Respuesta corta
rows: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.
Yes, you have. / No, you haven't.

explain.title: HAVE GOT o HAVE
explain.es: Have got es para tener cosas. Pero have solo (sin got) también sirve para acciones: desayunar, ducharse, pasarlo bien. En las acciones nunca va got.
explain.en: Have got = possession. Have (without got) is also used for actions. Actions never take got.

items.en: I've got a sister. Her name is Lucía.
items.es: Tengo una hermana. Se llama Lucía.

items.en: Our school has got a big playground.
items.es: Nuestro cole tiene un patio grande.

items.en: The elephant has got big ears.
My grandparents have got a farm.
Has your dog got a name?
Have you got a cold? — Yes, I have.
My cat hasn't got a tail.
Have your parents got a big car? — No, they haven't.
items.es: ¿Tus padres tienen un coche grande? — No.

items.bad: I have a dog. <small>(en el examen del cole)</small>
Do you have got a pen?
items.why: Con have got no se usa do.

items.bad: I no have got a cat.
items.why: En inglés no se niega con «no».
La respuesta corta va sin got.
La edad va con TO BE.

items.en: Find the subject: who has something?

items.es: ¿Es he, she, it (o un nombre como Mario, my mum, the cat)? → has. Si no → have.
items.en: he / she / it (or one name) → has. Others → have.
Positive → have/has got. Negative → haven't/hasn't got.

items.es: Repasa: ¿he puesto got? ¿Solo una vez y sin s?
items.en: Check: is got there, once, without s?

lines.en: Have you got a pet, Leo?
Yes, I have. I've got a rabbit.
Cool! Has it got long ears?
Yes, it has. And it's got a white tail.
lines.es: Sí. Y tiene una cola blanca.

lines.en: I haven't got a rabbit, but I've got a dog.
lines.es: Yo no tengo conejo, pero tengo un perro.

lines.en: Has your dog got a name?
Yes, it has. Its name is Rocky!

explain.title: Truco del sujeto
explain.es: Si puedes cambiar el sujeto por he, she o it, usa has. My mum → she → has got. The dogs → they → have got.
explain.en: If you can change the subject for he, she or it, use has.

text: Hi! I'm Mario. I'm eight years old. I've got a big family! I've got a sister, Lucía. She's twelve. She has got long brown hair and she has got glasses.

I haven't got a brother. We've got a dog. His name is Rocky. He has got a short tail and big ears. My grandparents have got a farm with two horses. My mum has got a blue car, but my dad hasn't got a car. He has got a bike!

I can give short answers without got.

checklist.es: Nunca escribo <s>has gots</s> ni <s>Do you have got</s>.

checklist.es: Digo mi edad con TO BE: I am nine.
